title: Una vez que: marcar el punto de partida de algo nuevo

sections.content: Una vez que (once, as soon as) marks the moment one thing is complete and something new begins as a result -- useful for historical narration moving from a turning-point event into what followed. It takes the indicative for a completed past event, the subjunctive for a future or hypothetical one. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Una vez que asumió el poder, el nuevo gobierno sandinista impulsó rápidamente una campaña de alfabetización nacional.
items.english: Once it took power, the new Sandinista government quickly launched a national literacy campaign.

items.spanish: Una vez consolidado el nuevo gobierno, no tardó en surgir una intensa oposición armada e internacional.
items.english: Once the new government was consolidated, intense armed and international opposition wasn't long in emerging.

items.spanish: Una vez que el Frente Sandinista logró derrocar a Somoza, comenzó el difícil trabajo de gobernar un país devastado por la guerra.
items.english: Once the Sandinista Front managed to overthrow Somoza, the difficult work of governing a war-devastated country began.

items.spanish: Una vez que se cumplan las condiciones acordadas, ambas partes podrán avanzar hacia una paz duradera.
items.english: Once the agreed conditions are met, both sides will be able to move toward a lasting peace.

sections.content: Una vez + past participle (una vez consolidado el gobierno) is a compact alternative to una vez que + verb -- both mean the same thing, but the participle form is more common in formal written narration.
